facts.claim: Demonstration uses nonlinear structured detection: spatial pump masks and frequency upconversion connect a MIR object to a single silicon detector.
Copper sheet carries four transmission letters, E/C/N/U. Pattern manufacture details and thickness are not given.

A double-polished silicon wafer with a laser-etched five-point star is a distinct transmission experiment. The closed qualified-service boundary is an authored requirement, not a reported source practice.
Signal, structured pump and upconverted detection bands are distinct.
The conversion channel, aperture and pump coverage limit imaging; these are not robot-interface dimensions.
Analog and photon-counting detector branches are separate configurations.
DMD pixel pitch is a device specification; reconstructed image grid is not achieved spatial resolution.
Main analog imaging compares experimental 16x16 and 64x64 letters with source numerical predictions. No source simulation is rerun here.
Dynamic analog demonstration has different resolution/rate settings; rates include acquisition and reconstruction.
facts.source: Main pp4-5; Media description; Movie2 labels

facts.claim: The full-Hadamard photon-sparse sweep pairs incident mean photons per pulse with per-displayed-mask accumulation.
Compressive random-pattern images use a 25% sampling ratio at 64x64. Denoised cases differ from un-denoised cases.
The integration sweep holds incident mean flux at one photon per pulse and changes exposure and output grid.
The silicon-star sweep is separate from the copper mask sweep.
The source establishes mask correspondence using an object-removed beam and applies a Gaussian-profile correction.
facts.source: Main Fig2 p4; SI Note4 pp6-7, FigS3

facts.claim: Raster, random and Hadamard encoding are compared at the same incident illumination power. Equal power does not establish equal total acquisition or detected-photon budgets.
Hadamard signed weights use consecutive complementary optical displays; FIFO transfer preserves sequence order.
facts.source: Main Methods p7; SI Note3 pp5-6 and Note5 p9

facts.claim: Source analog timing is 200 microseconds per displayed mask, giving a 5 kHz display cadence in this configuration.
The written source reports a 14.6 MHz laser repetition rate; photon flux refers to mean occupancy per pulse, not total photons in a reconstructed image.
No complete experiment-level replication plan, uncertainty budget, numerical image-quality acceptance thresholds or blinded diverse-object study is specified.
facts.source: Review of complete main and SI

facts.claim: Data and author-modified reconstruction code are available only on request; cited l1-MAGIC and DRUNet/DPIR do not provide the exact used versions or configuration.
facts.source: Main Data/Code p7; SI Note5 p9

facts.claim: Demonstrated objects are binary sparse targets; general-scene, biomedical, terahertz, depth and spectro-volumetric applications are prospective.
Prior publications carry additional synchronization, source-generation and photon-flux calibration details.

boundary: Reported operating facts are references, not hardware commands, inferred robot tolerances, or guaranteed evaluator outcomes. Laser construction, exposed alignment, and sample-fabrication recipes are intentionally not transcribed.
